validatedOpinion.sourceBoundaryReason: Per A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1, minor stylistic and atmospheric inference is tolerated, but asserting Flo's status as 'fiancée' concretizes an unconfirmed relationship outcome (that the proposal succeeded) beyond what the closed-world overview establishes, which only frames the proposal as a forthcoming event. This is a bounded, fixable relationship-status overstatement rather than a severe distortion of plot mechanics or an ending/reveal disclosure, so MINOR is appropriate. The rest of the copy (description, whyWatch, vibeSummary) stays well within authorized premise and classification bounds.

sourceEvidence.notes: Overview supports: Greg promised Flo he'd never lie again, decides to propose to her, must introduce his crooked father and ex-charm actress mother, and reopens his alibi agency with former accomplices to find presentable fake parents. This grounds description, whyWatch, vibeSummary, and most of curiosityHook.

The overview describes the proposal as a pending decision/action ('when he decides to propose'), not a completed and accepted engagement. Referring to Flo as 'his fiancée' asserts a specific relationship outcome (accepted proposal) not established by the source.

'old habits never truly stopped' is a fair characterization of the premise itself: the overview establishes Greg promised never to lie again yet is forced back into deception by reopening his alibi agency, so this reflects an already-authorized plot tension rather than a spoiler of a later reveal.
whyWatch correctly attributes direction to Philippe Lacheau (facts.director) and frames the film within Comedy/Family genres (facts.genres), consistent with facts.countries (France).

vibeSummary's 'light, comedic, and easy to follow... breezy' directly reflects the authorized emotionalWeight (light), moods (funny), attentionDemand (easy), and matches facts.runtimeMinutes (88 minutes).

validatedOpinion.uncertaintyNotes: It is plausible that within the film's timeline the proposal and acceptance occur very early, making 'fiancée' a reasonable shorthand for the bulk of the film's runtime; however, the authorized overview itself frames the proposal as pending, so this cannot be confirmed under the closed-world standard.
